translations.text: The discourse of the blessed Hippolytus on the end of the times, drawn from the holy books, concerning Christ and the Antichrist.
1. I am informing you, who are firmly established in that knowledge of yours, so that you may understand this matter which you have set before us out of love [?], O my brother Theophilus!
You have judged it worthy and proper to draw generously and ungrudgingly, as from a holy spring, in agreement with the divine books themselves; I will set before you what you desire.
And do not take delight in this merely by hearing it with your ears, but understand it with all your strength and look to the matter itself, so that you may be able to glorify God in every way,

so that this may be sustenance for you in this world, given by us without care and without hardship, and so that you may answer with a ready word concerning what is hard for many to understand and difficult to attain.

Now sow this in the breadth of your heart as in rich and pure soil, so that by it you may silence and restrain those who rise up to oppose the word of salvation. But I fear lest you should sow this before unbelieving and blaspheming tongues, for this is no small harm [?];
rather, spread it before God-fearing and believing people who wish to live with dignity, righteousness and fear. For it is not in vain that the blessed apostle teaches in what he wrote to Timothy:
"O Timothy, keep the faith with care, and avoid the new sounds of unbelief and the forms of the opponents, who have gone astray concerning the confession of the faith";
and again: "But you, my child, be strong in the grace of Jesus Christ,

and what you heard from me by the hand of many witnesses, confirm this to those faithful people who will be able to teach others also." So then, the blessed apostle undertook with fear this matter, which was not foreknown and revealed to all;
he foresaw by the Spirit that faith is not with everyone.
How much more so, then, if we hand over the words of God to the negligent, to corrupt and unworthy people?

2. For those blessed prophets became eyes for us, foreseeing by the hand of faith the counsel of the Word, for they told it to the generations that came after them as well, and they told us not only about things past,

but also about their own times and about things to come, so that a prophet should not be so called for one time only, but also for the things to come, through foretelling to us the things prepared, so that the prophet might be spoken of as a prophet.

For all these, strengthened by the spirit of prophecy and worthily honoured by the Word himself, were fitted together like some kind of lyre, having that yoke as a plectrum; struck by his hand, they told us what God wills,
for the prophets did not prophesy anything by their own power, make no mistake, nor did they proclaim what they themselves wished;
but first they understood rightly through the Word, and then through a vision it was made known to them to set it forth well,

Being sent in this way, they rightly spoke these things, for to them alone had this revelation come from God. And if it were not so, according to what word did those prophets prophesy as prophets? But as for what they foresaw by the Spirit concerning the things prepared, and told us,

those prophets were not speaking about anything past, which everyone would have seen, but they truly told us of the things to come, and so they are reckoned as prophets. For this reason, too, the prophets have from the beginning been called seers,
and we also, taught by those who spoke well, make our declaration;
not that by our own wisdom we undertake to utter anything new,

but we bring forward into the open the words and writings that have been set forth from the beginning, and we shed light on them for those who are able to believe rightly, so that there may be a common benefit on both sides:
to those who are diligent we rightly reveal the things to come, and to those who listen let us reveal the force of what has been said.

And since the labor and the contest now lie before us on both sides, let us declare these things without fail and without wavering, and let us bring those who listen to receive what has been said by hearing it faithfully. I implore you, be my fellow contender by praying to God.

3. Just as the Word of God, who was the Word from the beginning, was revealed beforehand to the blessed prophets, and now for our sake has appeared on earth even as a man, he reveals this to you; through him, by means of prayer, we are eager to attain to this inquiry.

But because in his mercy the Word ungrudgingly makes himself known to all the saints, truly by his own hand, that of all the saints, as a knowing helper for our benefit, understanding this human weakness, so that he may teach those who are ignorant and turn those who have gone astray to his true way, and those who seek in faith may easily find, and to those who are ready to knock at the doors with pure body and undefiled heart it may be opened at once. For he does not despise any of his servants, nor does he abhor them, as though anyone were unworthy of divine counsels;

nor does he hold the rich man in greater esteem and greater honor than the poor, nor does he despise the poor man for his poverty, nor does he reproach the barbarian [?] as senseless, nor does he cast out the eunuch as being only part of a man, nor does he cast out woman because of her womanhood and that sin of the beginning, nor does he revile men because of that transgression of the commandment. Rather, he has mercy on all, and he wills to save all, and he desires to make all perfect as sons of God, and he ordains all the saints to be one perfect man. For the Son of God is one, through whom we too, having attained by the Holy Spirit to that birth from above, all desire to come and arrive at the one perfect and heavenly man.

4. For the Word of God, without seed, took holy flesh from the holy virgin, which is like a bridegroom's adornment, and he has it upon the cross, and he mingled this mortal flesh with his own power, this corruptible with the incorruptible, and this weak with the strong, that he might save these lost men. And now the sufferings on the cross are called the Lord's loom, and the power of the Holy Spirit within it the warp, and the holy flesh woven in the Spirit the woof, and the thread is the graces that come from the love of Christ, which bind and join the two into one; the shuttle is the Word, and the workers are the fathers and prophets, who weave for Christ the perfect robe reaching to the ankles. By their hands they have shown us the Word, like a shuttle, and through them he weaves whatever the Father wills.

5. But now the time urges us on to the investigation of things to come, and these words spoken beforehand by the grace of God are enough. It is now necessary to bring forward from the divine books and to declare how and of what kind the coming of the Adversary will be,
in what days or at what time that one of darkness will appear, from where and from what race,

and what his name is, which is declared by the numbers of its several letters, and what the error of his people will be, and how he will gather them from the ends of the earth and raise up affliction and persecution against the saints, and in what manner he will glorify himself as God;
and what his end will be, and in what manner the coming of the Lord will appear from heaven, and how the judgment of this world by fire will take place,
and what the glory of the saints and the kingdom of heaven will be, those who will reign with Christ, and what the eternal punishment of the wicked by fire will be.
6. Now, as our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, the Son of the Lord, was foretold as a royal and glorious lion,
in like manner the Scriptures have also spoken beforehand of the Antichrist as a lion, because of his fierceness and tyranny.
For in all things the deceiver will make himself like the Son of God. Now Christ is called a lion, and the Antichrist is also called a lion;
Christ appeared as a lamb, and he too will appear in the same way as a lamb, but inwardly he will be a lurking wolf; the Savior came into the world, and he too will come in the same way;
the Lord sent out the apostles to all the Gentiles, and so too he will send out false apostles;
Christ gathered the scattered sheep, and so too he will gather the scattered people; Christ baptized those who believed in him, and he too will baptize;
the Lord appeared in the likeness of men, and he too will come in the likeness of men;
the Savior raised up his own flesh and showed it to us as a temple, and he will build the destroyed temple of Jerusalem.
These are his devices of deception, which I will also tell you hereafter; now come, and let us begin from the beginning.
7. For the blessed Jacob speaks those blessings and prophesies thus concerning our Lord and Savior:
"Judah, may your brothers praise you, and your hands be upon the shoulders of your enemies; may your father's sons bow down to you.
Judah is a lion's whelp; from the sprouting you came forth, my son; lying down he will sleep like a lion and like a lion's whelp, and who will raise him up?
Let not the ruler fail from Judah, nor the prince from his loins, until he comes to whom belongs what stands and is kept for him;
and he alone will be the hope of the Gentiles. He will bind his guard [?] to the vine, and the foal of the ass to the branch of the vine.
He will wash his garment in wine and his adornment in the blood of the grape.
His eyes are joyful with wine, and his teeth are white as milk."
8. Now I have set out this recitation for you, and I would like it to suffice; but since these words call us to speak and to speak again, let us not remain silent;
for those divine words are truly magnifying and able to bring benefit to souls.

For the prophet says "a lion's whelp" concerning Judah and David, and by that manifestation in the flesh he speaks of the Son of God. And when he said, "from the sprouting you came forth, son," he showed us that sprouted fruit from the holy Virgin, not born of seed but conceived by the Spirit,
and this like a plant sprung up from holy earth; Isaiah says: "A flower will spring up from the roots of Jesse, and a flower from him will spread out";
now Isaiah says "flower," and Jacob "plant," because the Word first sprouted in that holy womb and afterwards became a flower spread out.
And when he said, "lying down he will sleep like a lion and like a lion's whelp," he speaks of that brief, momentary sleep of Christ,
as Isaiah says: "How has that faithful city Zion become a harlot, in which righteousness slept, but which is now filled with murderers?"
And David likewise says: "I lay down, I slept, I awoke, for the Lord is my helper"; and by that scripture he shows us the sleep and the resurrection that took place.
And Jacob says: "Who will raise him up?" Who but the Father himself; in accordance with which Paul also says: "and of God the Father, who raised him from the dead."
9. And when he said: "Let not the ruler fail from Judah, nor the prince from his loins, until he comes to whom belongs what stands and awaits him,
and he will be the hope of the Gentiles," he says this of Christ, from that race of Judah, for he is the hope of us Gentiles,
for we await him to come down from heaven, whom, behold, we even now see by the power of faith.
10. And when he said, "He will bind his guard [?] to the vine," this means that from the circumcision he assigns to that people of his that appointment of his, for he himself is that vine.

When he said, "that foal to the branch of the vine," this means that he joins the people of the Gentiles, like a young colt to its mother, uniting the circumcision and the uncircumcision together in faith by the calling.

11. And when he said, "He will wash that adornment in wine," he speaks of the descent of the Holy Spirit upon the Jordan, of that paternal grace. "And his garment in the blood of the grape": now what blood of the grape does he mean, if not that of his holy flesh, crushed like a cluster upon the cross,
from whose side came forth two springs, of blood and of water, by which the Gentiles are washed and purified, who are reckoned as ornaments to Christ.
12. "His eyes are joyful as with wine": who are the eyes of the Lord but those blessed prophets,
who foresaw in the Spirit and proclaimed beforehand? For in this way, perfected and strengthened, they rejoiced, because they beheld him there with that spiritual eye.
perfected by the Word himself and by his own graces.
13. And as for what he said, "His teeth are white as milk": this is because the commandments came forth from that holy mouth of Christ; and he likened them to something white, as milk is.
14. And now, since Christ is spoken of beforehand in the scriptures as a lion and a lion's whelp,
you will likewise find the same said of Antichrist. For Moses says: "Dan is a lion's whelp, and he shall begin to leap forth from Bashan."
But let no one be misled into thinking that he is speaking of Christ. Examine this well and diligently.
For in saying "Dan is a lion's whelp," he made known the tribe of Dan, the one now before us, from which the tyrant is destined to be born;
for just as in type our Savior was born from the tribe of Judah, so too the tyrant will be born from the tribe of Dan.
And that this is so, see what Jacob says: "Let Dan be a serpent lying in ambush on the road, to strike the heels of the horse."
Now who is the serpent but the one who has been the deceiver from the beginning, of whom Genesis speaks, who deceived Eve and overthrew Adam?
And now, since we must set this forth with many testimonies of the scriptures, let us not cease from them.
15. And since from that tribe of Dan a harsh king and wicked judge, the son of the deceiver, is destined to come and to arise, the prophet speaks thus:
"Dan shall judge his own people, as one tribe of Israel."
If someone should say that this was said about Samson, who was born of the tribe of Dan and judged the people for only twenty years,
then indeed a part of it is seen [?] in Samson, but it is fulfilled completely in Antichrist;
for the prophet Jeremiah too speaks thus: "The swiftness from Dan was heard, the speed of his horses;

at the sound of the neighing of his war-horses the whole earth shook." Again, another prophet also says: "He shall gather all his forces from the east as far as the west; those whom he calls and those whom he does not call shall gather to him;
he shall whiten the sea with the sails of his ships and blacken the land with his shields and armor, and everyone who meets him in battle shall fall by the blade of the sword."
And now he has said this about no one else but that arrogant, God-fighting tyrant, as I shall show you hereafter.
16. For Isaiah also says: "And it shall be, when the Lord has accomplished all that is to be done on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem,
he shall send [judgment] upon their great minds, and upon the rulers of Assyria, and upon the arrogance of the glory of his eyes, because of him;
for he said: By my strength I will do this, and by the knowledge of my counsel I will seize the boundaries of the nations and lay waste their strength;
I will shake inhabited cities, and I have taken the whole world in my hand like a nest, and I will gather them up like abandoned eggs;
No one will escape from me, and no one will turn to oppose me to my face. Is it not so?
But the Lord Adonai will send dishonor upon that honor of yours, and a consuming fire will blaze up upon that glory of yours,
and the light of Israel will be a fire to you, and will destroy you with its flame of fire, and will devour your might like hay."

17. And in another place he says: "How has that mighty one fallen silent, and how has that destroyer ceased? God has shattered the yoke of those rulers; he struck down that race with incurable torment and scourged it with the wrath of his indignation, and he had no mercy."
The whole world has rested in hope, and they rejoiced with gladness, and the tree of Lebanon was glad over you, and the fir of Lebanon;
since you fell asleep, no one has come up to cut us down. Hell below was embittered at meeting you, all together;
all the mighty ones who held power on the earth have risen; all the kings of the nations have risen from their thrones. All of them will answer and say to you:
You too have been seized, as we were, and you have been counted among us. Your glory and your gladness have gone down to hell;

beneath you they will spread rottenness, and your remains will be worms. How has that star which used to shine forth at dawn fallen from heaven, and how has he who used to send out to all the pagan nations been shattered upon the earth?
You said in your heart: I will go up to heaven, and above the stars I will set up my thrones;
I will sit on a high mountain, and upon the summits of the high mountains that are in the north; I will go up above the clouds, I will be like the Most High.
But now you will go down as far as hell and to the lowest depths of the earth. Those who see you will marvel at you and say:
This is the man who made the whole earth tremble and stirred it up, who made the whole world a wilderness and laid waste all the cities and did not release the captives.
All the rulers of the earth have fallen asleep in honor, each man in his own dwelling;
but you were cast out upon the mountains like a loathsome carcass, among the many fallen by the sword, who went down to hell.
Just as a garment stained with blood is not clean, so you too were not clean, for you destroyed my land and killed my people.
You will not stand for all time. Prepare your children for slaughter for the sins of your father, so that they may not rise up and inherit the land."
18. And the prophet Ezekiel speaks of him thus: "Thus says the Lord God: Because you exalted yourself in your heart and said, 'I am God, and my dwelling is in the heart of the sea,'
yet you are a man and not God, and you made your heart like the heart of God; are you then wiser than Daniel?
And have the learned not taught you by their counsel? Was it by the wisdom of your own counsel that you gathered for yourself power, and gold and silver into your treasuries?
Or was it by the great knowledge of your soul that you multiplied your power? Your heart was exalted by your pride, and now thus says the Lord God:
Because you made your heart like the heart of God, behold, I will raise up against you foreign and ruthless pagans,
and they will bring their swords against you and against the beauty of your counsel, and they will give your beauty over to destruction,
and they will strike you down, and you will die a death at the hands of those who wound you, in the heart of the sea.
You said: 'I am a god before those who slay you'; but you are ash and not a god. By the multitude of the uncircumcised you shall perish at the hand of foreigners, for I say this, said the Lord."

19. Now, after what has been said, let us look closely at what Daniel says in his visions. He gives a determination concerning those who were to arise as kings after these, and he has shown us; at the end of the times he assigned the coming of the assailant and the end of this whole world.
Now he sets forth the vision of Nebuchadnezzar: "You, O king, were looking, and behold, an idol stood before you, whose head was of pure gold,
its arms and shoulders of silver, its belly and thighs of bronze, its shins of iron, its feet of iron and clay.
You were watching, and a stone was cut out without any hand touching it, and it struck the idol that stood upon the feet of iron and clay, and crushed it completely.

At that time the clay and the iron and the bronze and the silver and the gold were shattered, and became like the dust of a threshing floor in the days of summer [?], and the force of the winds carried it away, and not even its place was found. And the stone that crushed the idol became a great mountain and filled the ends of heaven."

20. Now let us compare with this the corresponding vision of Daniel and show that the two have one meaning, so that they may be alike in unity with one another and true. For Daniel says thus: "I was looking, and behold, four winds from heaven were let down upon the great sea, and four great beasts came up out of the sea, of various colors. The first was a lioness, and its wings were like those of an eagle. I was looking until its wings fell off, and it was lifted up from the earth, and it walked as on the feet of a man, and the heart of a man was given to it. And behold, the second beast, like a bear. And it stood apart on one side, and there were three ribs in its mouth. I was looking, and behold, another beast like a leopard, with four wings on its shoulders like those of a bird, and the beast had four heads. After this I was looking, and behold, the fourth beast, terrible and exceedingly strong; its teeth were of iron and its claws of bronze.

It devoured and crushed, and trampled what remained with its foot. And it turned about, and was more terrible than the other beasts that were before it. And there were ten horns upon it. And I was looking at its horns, and behold, another small horn came up among them, and three of the horns were plucked out before it. And there were eyes like those of a man in that horn, and a mouth, and it spoke great things.

21. "I was looking until thrones were set in place and the Ancient of Days sat down. His clothing was white as snow, and the hair of his head like pure wool; his throne was like a flame of fire, and the wheels of his chariots were burning fire.
A river of fire flowed before him; thousands of thousands served him, and myriads of myriads stood around him. The court was set and the records were opened.

[?] at that time because of the sound of the great words that the horn was speaking, until the beast fell and was destroyed and its flesh was given to the fire to be burned; and the dominion of the other beasts also was changed.
22. "I was looking in a vision of the night, and behold, with the clouds of heaven, a son of man coming,
and he came to the Ancient of Days,
and to him was given dominion and honor and kingship; all peoples, tribes, and tongues shall serve him;
his dominion is a dominion forever, and his kingdom shall not pass away."
23. Now, since it seems difficult to some to understand the force of this saying, I will not withhold any of these things from being made known to those who are of lively mind.
And as for what he said, "A lioness came up out of the sea," he said this about the king of the Babylonians, and this is the head of gold of that idol;
and as for what he said, "Its wings were like an eagle's," it is because Nebuchadnezzar rose up as king and grew arrogant toward God;
and as for what he said, "Its wings fell off," this means that his dominion was taken away and he was driven out.
And as for what he said, "The heart of a man was given to it," this means that he understood and repented, recognizing of himself that he is a man, and gave glory to God.
24. And after this, as for what he said, "I saw the second beast, like a bear," these are the Persians; and as for what he said,
"Three ribs [?] in its mouth," he has shown us the three peoples, of the Persians and the Medes and the Babylonians; this is, after the gold, the silver in that idol.
The third beast, these are the Elamites, for after the Persians Alexander of Macedon conquered and struck down Darius; this is what was the bronze in that idol.
And what he said, "The four wings of a bird and the four heads of that beast," clearly shows us how the kingdom of Alexander was divided into four parts; and as for what he said,
"Four heads," he speaks of the four kings who came from him,
for at the end of Alexander the kingdom was divided into four parts.
25. And as for what he said, "The fourth beast, terrible, its teeth like iron and its claws like bronze,"
who then are these but the Romans, and this is the iron, who now hold dominion? For "its shins are of iron."
And now after this, what remains for us to examine, beloved, except the figure of the feet of that idol, part of which was of iron and part of clay, mixed with one another?
In a saying he shows us, by the toes of the feet, the ten kings who are to arise from it, of whom Daniel says:
"I watched that beast, and behold, ten horns on its head, from among which another sprang up, and three of them it destroyed,"
which is none other than the Antichrist, who is to arise; and he shall restore the kingdom of the Jews. And as for the three horns, of which he says that they were [?] uprooted,
he shows us the three kings, of Egypt and of the Libyans and of the Ethiopians,

whom he shall strike down in battle, and they shall become [?] to him; for he shall be fierce, [?] and arrogant, and shall bring affliction and persecution upon the saints; for he shall exalt himself over them.
For Daniel says: "I watched those horns, and behold, that horn made war against the saints and prevailed over them,
until that beast was destroyed and perished; its body was given over to the fire to be burned."
26. After whom shall appear from heaven the one who is the stone that struck that idol and ground it to powder, and overturned every kingdom and gave the reign to the saints of the Most High;
This is the one who "became a great mountain and filled all the ends of heaven," concerning whom Daniel says: "I was seeing a vision of the night,
and behold, with the clouds of heaven one like a son of man was coming, and he reached the Ancient of Days.
And to him was given authority and honor and dominion, and all peoples, tribes and every language were serving him;
his reign is a reign forever, and his dominion will not be destroyed." For he has shown us that all authority has been given by the Father to the Son,
who is king of the heavens and of the earth and of the netherworld, and judge of all:
of the heavens, in that the Word was from the heart of the Father before all things; and of the things of earth, because he was born as a man from man, by a birth from above, his own Adam [?];
and of the netherworld, in that he was counted among the dead, both by bringing good news to the holy souls and by conquering death through death.
27. Now of all these things, and of the ten toes of the idol, which were a figure of the rule over the world,
and of the ten horns of the beast, divided into ten parts, let us clearly understand what has been set forth here, and see it compared.
28. The head of the idol, of gold, and the lioness were the Babylonians, the [?]; and the arms of silver and the bear are the Persians and Medes;
the belly and thighs of bronze and the leopard are the Elamites, who took power from Alexander; the shins of iron and the terrible beast are the Romans, who now hold power;
and the toes of the feet, clay and iron, and what are the horns that are prepared to come into being? And the other horn that will rise up from among them is the Antichrist;
the stone that struck the idol and crushed it, and that filled the earth, is Christ, by his manifestation from heaven and his coming upon the world for judgment.
29. Beloved, I make this known to you with fear, for the sake of the immeasurable love of Christ;
and the blessed prophets who were before us knew it and did not dare to declare it openly, so that no stumbling should befall the sons of men, but they made it known to us by hints, in parable, [?],
telling us what they knew with understanding in their minds; how much greater, then, is this labor for us, since we are making known to you openly, by comparison, what they spoke in hints!
Now see what is to befall the wicked, the unbelieving and the defiled at the end, and in what manner the wrath of God will come upon them before the judgment, the torment that has been prepared.

30. Awake, arise, come forward, blessed Isaiah, tell me plainly what you prophesy concerning the great city of Babylon. For you spoke also about Jerusalem, and behold, it has been fulfilled; for you spoke to her openly and without fear:
"Your land is desolate, your cities burned with fire; strangers devour your countryside before you; it is laid waste and overthrown by strangers;
the daughter of Zion will be left behind and abandoned like a tent of [?], and like the bed of fruit-keepers in a melon field, and like a besieged city."
Now behold, has not all this come to pass? For the things spoken by you have been fulfilled.
Has not the land of Judea been laid waste? Has not the sanctuary been burned with fire? Have not the walls been overthrown?
Have those cities not been brought low? Do strangers not devour their land? Is the land not held by the Romans?
For this reason those lawless ones hated you, and they were destroyed because they crucified Christ. You died with Christ, but you are alive with him.
31. Now which of you shall I love more? But likewise I too [?] was stoned; likewise Daniel too bears witness.
And you, Daniel, should I praise you above all? But John too does not lie, and all the more that word which was spoken to you.
For you died with Christ, but you are alive with God. Listen and rejoice: behold, the things you narrated, which came to pass in those times, have been fulfilled.
For you saw these things first, and then afterward you likewise proclaimed those words of God to all generations and made them known to all generations.

You appeared as prophets so that you might be able to save all, so that in this way the true prophet may be reckoned as a prophet, when he foretells the things appointed to come and also shows us those that are past.

You have all become disciples of the good teacher; therefore I speak to you as to the living and the worthy, for behold, you also have that crown of life and incorruption, which stands ready and is kept for you, that heavenly crown.
32. Tell me, O blessed Daniel, set my mind at rest, I beseech you: prophesy concerning the lioness, for you were a captive.

Tell me also the things appointed to come, concerning the bear, for you were in the world and saw this come to pass; and then afterward you tell me about the leopard. And from where did this knowledge of what was to come reach you?
For behold, you had fallen asleep at that time. Who taught you this, if not the one who formed you in your mother's womb, the Word?
For you spoke and did not lie, for the leopard arose, the he-goat came, struck the ram, broke his horns and trampled him underfoot,
and he stood and was exalted; and at his fall four horns sprang up from him. Rejoice, blessed Daniel, you did not err; all this has come to pass.
33. And after this you tell us about the fourth beast: "Terrible and dreadful, its teeth of iron and its claws of bronze;
it devours and crushes to pieces, and tramples the remainder with its feet";
and that the iron now holds power, and that it shatters everything and crushes it to pieces, and that it has subdued those who were unwilling,
and that we see these things, and that we glorify God, having been taught by you.
34. But since the matter of the wicked one lies before us, stand forth and speak, O blessed Isaiah; let us see what he says about Babylon:
"Come down, sit on the ground, O virgin daughter of Babylon;

sit, O daughter of the Chaldeans; you shall no longer be called delicate and tender. Take the millstones and grind flour; strip off your veil [?], gather up your grey hairs, show your legs, cross over the river. Your shame shall be seen; your reproaches shall be exposed; for the due penalty will be exacted from you,
and I will no longer give you into the hands of men, says the one who redeemed you,
the Lord Sabaoth, the Holy One of Israel. Sit down undone, go into the darkness, you daughter of the Chaldeans, and you shall no longer be called the might of kingship.
35. "You provoked me to anger against my people, you defiled my inheritance; I gave them into your hands, and you showed them no mercy, not even to a single one of them;
you made the yoke of the old man very heavy and said: My dominion shall last forever. You did not understand in your heart, and you did not remember what would come afterward.
Hear this, you who sit in luxury, you who trust in yourself and say: I am, and there is no one else besides me; I shall not sit as a widow, and I shall not know orphanhood.
But now both of these shall come upon you in one day,
widowhood and childlessness shall come upon you suddenly, for your sorcery, for the strength of your enchanters and your sorcerers, and for the multitude of your harlotry; for you said: I am.
And there is no one else. And your adultery shall be your shame, for you said in your heart: I am.
And destruction shall come upon you, and you will not understand it; and they shall dig a pit before you, and you shall fall into it.
And poverty shall come upon you, and you shall no longer be justified.

And a snare shall come upon you, and you will not understand it; and you trusted in the hands of enchanters and sorcerers and in the multitude of your sorcery, which you have followed from your youth, and which have brought you no profit. You have worn yourself out with your counsels; now stand, and let those star-enchanters save you, those who practice enchantment by the stars, let them tell you what is prepared to come upon you.
For behold, all of them shall be burned by fire like stubble, and they shall not be able to deliver their own souls from the flame, for you have spread out coals of fire;
sit upon it, and it shall be a help to you; you have wearied yourself with trafficking from your youth;
each man has gone astray on his own way, and for you there shall be no more salvation." This, then, is what Isaiah says about this; and let us see whether John cries out in the same way as he does.
36. For he was on the island of Patmos, and he saw a vision of awesome mysteries; and by recounting them generously and ungrudgingly he teaches others as well.
Tell me, O blessed John, apostle and witness of the Lord, what did you see or what did you hear concerning Babylon? Awake and speak, for she is the one who banishes you and drives you away in wrath.
And he said: "One of the seven angels who had the seven cups came, and spoke with me and said to me:

Come, I will show you the torment of the great harlot, who has come and sits upon many waters, with whom the kings of the earth defiled themselves, and the inhabitants of the earth became drunk from her harlotry.
And he brought me into the desert by the Holy Spirit; and I saw a woman upon beasts, worm [?], and it had names [?], seven heads and horns [?].
And the woman was clothed in scarlet and purple and gilded with gold, with precious stone and pearl, and she had in her hand a cup full of abominations and the filth of the idolatry of the earth;
and on her forehead was written a mystery: Babylon the great, the mother of harlots and of the abominations of the earth.
37. "And I saw the woman drunk with that of the saints and with the blood of Jesus; and when I saw her, I marveled and grew faint; and the angel said to me: Why did you marvel?
I will tell you the mystery of the woman and concerning the beast that holds her, to which belong the seven heads and the ten horns.
And the beast that you saw was and is not; it is ready to come up out of the abysses and to go to perdition.
And the inhabitants of the earth, whose names have not been written in the books of the living from the beginning of the world, will marvel at the beast that you saw, which was and is not.
38. "And here is understanding for the one who has knowledge. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits, and they are seven kings;
the five have passed away, the one is, the other has not yet come, and when he comes, he will remain for only a short time.
And the beast that was and is not, he himself is the fourth, and is of the seven, and he will go to perdition.

And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have not yet taken hold of dominion, but authority will be given to them as kings for one hour together with the beast. These will be of one will and will have one power, and they will assign their authority to the beast. These will make war on the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for he is Lord of lordships and King of kings,
and those who are called to him are chosen and faithful.

39. "And he said to me: The waters that you were looking at, where the harlot sits, are many peoples and tribes and nations. And the ten horns that you were looking at, and the beast, these will come to hate the harlot and will leave her deserted and desolate, stripped naked,
and they will eat her flesh and burn her with fire.
For God has put it into their heart to carry out his will, and they will be of one will,
and they will give their authority to the beast until the words of God are fulfilled. And the woman whom you saw is the great city Babylon, which has authority over the kings of the earth.
40. "After this I saw another angel coming down from heaven, who had great authority, and the earth was illuminated

by his glory. He cried out with a great voice and said: Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and she has become a dwelling place of demons and a refuge of base [?], unclean, wicked and loathsome things; for by the wrath of her drunkenness all the Gentiles have fallen,
and the kings of the earth have defiled themselves with her, and the rulers of the earth have grown wanton from the abundance of her power.
And I heard a voice from heaven above, and it said: Come out of her, you my people, so that you may not have a share in her sins;
and do not receive a share in her punishment, for her sins have piled up as far as heaven, and God has remembered her lawless deeds.
41. "Repay her as she has done to you, and punish her twofold according to her deeds. Give her to drink from the very cup from which she gave you to drink.
As much as she has glorified herself and grown wanton, so much torment and mourning inflict on her, for she says in her heart: I sit as queen, and I am not a widow, and I shall not be in mourning.
Therefore in one day death and mourning will come upon her, and she will be burned up with fire; for mighty is the Lord who will judge her.

And the kings of the earth who defiled themselves with her and extolled her in wickedness will see and will weep over her, when they see the smoke rising from her burning. They will stand far off for fear of her torments, and they will say:
Woe, woe, the great city Babylon, the mighty city, for in one day your punishments have come! And the merchants of the earth were weeping and mourning over her,
for no one will buy their wares any more, wares of gold and silver,
of precious stones, and pearl, and fine linen,

and scarlet, and silk, and purple, and all thyine wood, and every vessel of ivory, and every vessel of precious woods, and of bronze, and of iron, and of marble, and cinnamon, and incense, and ointment,
and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and wheat, and cattle, and sheep, and horses for chariots and for riding, for the use of men.
And the fruit you desired has gone from you, and you will find it no more.
Her merchants, who were made great by her, stood far off for fear of her torments, and with weeping and mourning they said:
Woe, that great city, which was clothed in fine linen and scarlet and purple, and adorned with gold and precious stone and pearl, for in one hour all that wealth has been laid waste.
And all the shipmen, and all the various people on the ships, and all who travel on the sea stood far off and cried out, and they watched the smoke rising from her burning and will say:
Who is like that great city Babylon? And they will throw dust on their heads and lament with weeping and grief, and say:
Woe, woe, the great city, by whose costly wealth those who traveled the sea by ship grew rich, for in one hour they have been laid waste.
42. "Rejoice over her, you heavens, and you holy prophets and apostles, for God has passed your judgment upon her."
And one angel took up a stone like a great millstone and threw it into the sea and said: Thus Babylon, that great city, will be thrown down and sunk, and will be found no more.
And the sound of the lyre and of singers and of pipes will be heard from you no more;
and all the skill of craftsmen will be found in you no more; and the sound of the mill will be heard from you no more; and the light of a lamp will be found in you no more;
and the voice of bridegroom and bride will be heard from you no more; for your merchants were the great ones of the earth, for by your sorcery you led all nations astray;
and in you was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all who were slain by you."

43. Now, concerning those torments and what is to come upon her at the end of the times from those who are to arise as tyrants in those times, this passage plainly reveals the judgment apportioned to her.

It is also necessary for us to show truly the time, at what time this will be, and how that little horn will spring up among them. For the iron shins, which hold sway even now, reach down to the feet, ankles and toes, in accordance with the likeness of that image as it appeared and of that beast terrible to behold, as was made known to us beforehand in figure, at the time when the iron and the clay will be mixed together.

And Daniel shows us what lies before us, for he said: "He will make a covenant with many for one week, and it will be that in the half of the week vows and sacrifices will be abolished." Now that one part of the week, which is to be at the end of the whole world, he has revealed, the half of which week they will take up;
And the two prophets, Enoch and Elijah: for they will preach "one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed with power," and will give repentance to the people and to all the Gentiles.
44. And they will proclaim the two comings of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, as was made known to us through the prophets: the first, in the likeness of the flesh, despised;
"And he had neither appearance nor beauty, but his appearance was despised and dishonored above all men; a man in affliction, and he knows how to endure pains; he was reviled and not esteemed."
But his second coming is proclaimed with glory, how he will come from heaven with power and with angels and with the glory of the Father, as the prophet says:

"You shall see the king in glory," and as he said: "I was watching, and upon the clouds one like a son of man was coming, and he came as far as the Ancient of Days, and to him were given honor and glory and kingship over all;
all tribes and languages shall serve him; his kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, which shall not be destroyed."

For this reason also there are two forerunners and heralds. The first herald, John the son of Zechariah, became in all things the forerunner and herald of the Savior, and by spreading abroad to all the light of salvation manifested in the world;
for he began to run ahead in his mother's womb, and was born beforehand of Elizabeth,
so that even to those who were infants in their mothers' wombs he might show the one who was to come, the new one to be born by the Holy Spirit of the virgin.
45. He heard the greeting of Mary, for he leapt with joy in his mother's womb, because he saw the Word of God conceived.

And then he went out into the wilderness preaching, telling the people of the baptism of repentance, and announcing beforehand salvation to the Gentiles, who had been scattered in the world as in a wilderness.
After this, at the Jordan, he showed the Savior face to face and said: "Behold the Lamb of God, who will take away the sins of the world."

For he was the first to reach those who were in hell, to preach to them, having been killed by Herod after being a herald; and there he announced the prepared descent of the Lord for those who were to be redeemed, by the redemption of the holy souls from the hands of death.
46. But since the Savior was the beginning of the resurrection, and since it was appointed for the Lord alone to rise from the dead, through whom judgment is to come upon the whole world;
for those who have labored worthily shall also be worthily glorified by him, by that good fellow-contender, who first of the contests
completed them and sat in heaven at the right hand of God the Father,
and will then be manifested as judge at the end of the world. It is necessary that his heralds also come beforehand, for he says well through the prophet Malachi:

"I will send you Elijah the Tishbite before the coming of that great and appointed day of the Lord, who will turn the hearts of the fathers toward the children, and the disobedient to the knowledge of righteousness,
lest I come and strike the earth altogether." Now these will come and preach about the things that are prepared and are to be, about the manifestation of Christ from heaven,
who will also perform miracles and signs. Who knows whether they may perhaps restrain people and turn them to repentance, because of their exceeding wickedness and lawlessness?

47. For John also says: "I will grant to those two witnesses of mine, who will prophesy, one thousand two hundred and sixty days, clothed in sackcloth." This is that part of the week of which Daniel spoke.

"These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands that stand before the Lord of the earth. And if anyone wishes to harm them, fire will come out of their mouth and devour their enemies. These will have power to shut

the sky, so that there may be no rain during the days of prophecy; and they will have authority over the waters, to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.
"And when they complete their course and their testimony" -- what does the prophet say?

-- "The beast that came up out of the sea will make war on them and overcome them and kill them," because they will refuse to give glory to the Adversary [?]; this is he who came up, that little horn.
He will lift up his heart, will be exalted, and will magnify himself as God; he will persecute the saints and blaspheme Christ, as Daniel says:

"I was watching that horn, and behold, there were eyes like those of a man, and there was a mouth, and it spoke great things; and it opened its mouth to blaspheme God. And that horn made war against the saints and grew strong over them,
until that beast was destroyed and perished, and its body was given to the fire to be burned."
48. But since it is necessary for us to inquire fully about him and to give an account, and to tell how the Holy Spirit reveals even his name by a certain number, let us tell you about it plainly.
For John speaks thus: "And I saw another beast coming up out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
And it exercised the authority of the first beast before it, and it will compel the earth and its inhabitants to worship that first beast,
whose wound was healed. And it will perform great signs, for it will even make fire rain, as it were, from heaven to earth before people's eyes.

And it will deceive the inhabitants of the earth by the signs that were given to it to perform before the beast, for it will tell the inhabitants of the earth to make an image of the beast that had the wound by the sword and stood.
And spirit was given to the image of the beast, and it will be that those who do not worship the image of the beast will be killed.
And it will make its own the small and the great, the despised and the destitute, the free and the slaves,
so that they may put a mark on their right hand and on their forehead, so that no one who does not have as a sign the name of the beast, or else the number of the calling [?] of

its [name], may be permitted either to buy or to sell. Here is understanding: let the one who has a mind know by number the name of the beast, for it is a man's number, and its number in the language of the Georgians is six hundred [285 ?] sixty and one."
49. Now by the beast that came up out of the earth he means the dominion of the Adversary [?], which is to arise;
and by the two horns, him and the one who is the false prophet with him.

And as for what he said, "The horns were like those of a lamb": it is because he intends to make himself like the Son of God, exalting himself by his own doing. And as for what he said, that he spoke like a dragon: it is because he is a deceiver and is not true.
"And he will exercise all the authority of the first beast, and he will make the earth and its inhabitants worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed."
By this he foretells to us that, like the law of Augustus by which the kingdom of the Romans was established, so too this one will prevail and will issue commands by edicts, exalting himself.
For this is the fourth beast, whose head was crushed and then healed, on account of its dissolution and dishonor and division into ten parts,
he being indeed crafty, and as though it would be healed and renewed.
For this was said by the prophet [?]: "For he will give breath to that idol, and the image of the beast will speak":
because he set to work and grew strong, but by God, the discerning one, he was crushed and tormented, and became food for worms, and departed from this life.
And if anyone wishes to understand this fully, it is written in "the Maccabees."

50. But now, what lies before us, of this we shall speak. For he too will oppress the saints in the same manner, for the prophet and apostle says thus: "Let him who has understanding reckon by number the name of the beast,
for it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred and sixty-one."
But now, concerning his name, we find nothing that we can state with truth;

but we have not been able to understand it, though it was made known to us concerning him by the blessed John; and, as we suppose, at his appearing time will reveal this thing that is sought; for as much as we understand, let us speak of it haltingly.
Now we find many names of his that fall under that number,
and, this being so, come, let us state the one that is the most ancient of all, his name from the beginning;
for this name resolves into that same number, and many other names too are found that fit it.
But as we said before, that the wound of the first beast was healed and that, grown strong, it will speak,
it is manifest that those who hold it until this present time are the Latins; now let it be transferred to the name of one man: Latinos;

Now this must be said beforehand with caution, because this is easy, and one must not be ignorant, for it is not possible to say anything else, but only to lay up the counsel of God in the heart, kept with fear and with honor, for, of the blessed
prophets, this saying concerns what has been and what will be, by foreknowledge; let us not go astray.
For when that time has come, and he himself concerning whom this was said has appeared, this name will be made known doubly to all.
51. And so that we may bring into submission, not by this word alone, those who read the commands of God, let us show it also from what was said by others.

For Daniel says: "And these are the ones who will escape from his hands: Edom and Moab and the sons of Ammon"; for these are the ones who will be helpers to him because of their kinship and because of his appearing as king over them.
For the Idumeans are the sons of Esau, and Ammon and Moab are those who were children of the two daughters of Lot, whose race stands until now and waits. For Isaiah says:
"And they will fly in the ships of the foreigners on the sea, and those who are from the east, for Moab will first be under his hand, and the two sons of Ammon will submit to him."
52. Now this one, at that time, because of them, will be appointed and victorious in the contest of battle against the three horns uprooted from among the ten,

who are the Egyptians, Libyans and Ethiopians. He will plunder and destroy them, and over the other seven remaining horns he will begin to exalt himself in his heart and to grow insolent toward God, as though he ruled over the whole world.
And his advance will first be against Tyre and Berytus and the surrounding lands;
for first, because of their fall, terror and fear will come upon the others, as Isaiah says: "Be ashamed, Sidon, said the sea, and the strength of the sea said:
I have not been in labor and I have not given birth, and I have not reared young men, nor have I brought up virgins;
but when Egypt hears, pain will seize them because of Tyre."
53. Now concerning the things to come, beloved, and the three horns uprooted directly after them: he will begin over them also to show himself as God, as Ezekiel foretold:
"Because you have exalted yourself in your heart and said: I am God"; and Isaiah likewise says: "You said in your heart:
I will ascend to heaven and set my thrones above the stars, and I will be like the Most High; but now you will go down to hell and to the depths of the earth";
and Ezekiel says: "You will say to those who slay you: I am God; but you are a man and not God."

54. Now, concerning these words that have been revealed, and concerning his race, his manifestation, his destruction, and his name, which has been indicated by reasoning, let us also consider his deeds.
For he will call all that people and gather those scattered from all lands, claiming them there as his own children,
and to build the city and to raise the temple for them; for he will receive from them something like worship, as the prophet says:
"He will gather all his power from the east to the west; those whom he calls and those whom he does not call will go to him";
and Jeremiah presents a parable and says thus: "The partridge called out and gathered chicks that it did not hatch,
making its wealth unjustly, and in the middle of its days they will abandon it, and at its end it will be a fool."

55. Now it will do no harm to the matter set before us, for it tells us the nature of the creature; for this reason the prophet did not disclose the nature of that creature in vain, presenting it in a parable.

As for the partridge, it is a vain boaster: when it sees the chicks of another partridge flown off alone to feed, it imitates the voice of their father, who is a stranger to it, and calls to the other bird's chicks; and they think it is their own father and run to it. And it [?] them and goes around among the strange chicks as if they were its own. But when the true father arrives and calls with his own voice, the chicks recognize it, abandon the new one, and go to the true father.

In the same way the prophet speaks about the Antichrist: for he calls humankind to himself, wanting to make strangers his own, and he promises salvation to all in vain, while he will be unable to save even himself.

56. Now when he has gathered those peoples who at all times are disobedient to God, he, being worshipped by them, will begin to persecute the saints, who are his enemies and adversaries, as the Savior says: "There was a judge in a city who did not fear God and had no shame before men; and there was a widow in that same city, and she kept entreating him and saying to him: Give me justice against my adversary. But he would not listen for some time;
and afterward he came to himself and said: Even if I do not fear God and have no shame before men, yet because this widow continually wearies me, for this reason I will give her justice."

57. Now that judge of falsehood, who did not fear God and had no shame before men, is truly said of the Antichrist; for he is a son of the devil, and he will begin to wield power and to rise up against the face of God, he who indeed neither fears God nor has shame before men, and who will supposedly be judge of all together. And as for the widow who he says was in that city, he means Jerusalem itself, which until now is a widow, having abandoned her heavenly Bridegroom; she seeks vengeance through one mortal man, as though to be saved from Christ as from an adversary at law and not a Savior, not having understood the saying of the prophet Jeremiah: "Because they did not obey the truth, then deception will speak to that people and to Jerusalem"; and Isaiah likewise: "Because that people did not wish to drink the water of Siloam which flows quietly, but chose as king over them Rezin, king of the Assyrians"; and by the king of the Assyrians he speaks figuratively of the Antichrist, as another prophet also says: "And this shall be peace from me: when the Assyrian comes into your land and reaches your border."
58. And Moses too says the same, foretelling that it is prepared not to obey but to depart from and cast off the true Savior of the world,
and to obey the deceiver, the king of the earth, and to despise the heavenly one;
he says thus: "Behold, is not all this gathered up by me and sealed, kept in my treasury? On the day of vengeance I will repay them, at the time when their feet slip."

Now they went astray in everything, and were not found in unity with the truth in any one thing: neither in the law, for they became transgressors of the law, nor yet through the prophets, for they killed them,

nor in the time of the Gospel, for they crucified the Savior himself, nor did they obey the apostles, for they handed them over to death, having at all times been those who drive away and revile the truth, haters of God rather than lovers of God; to whom it will be repaid in like manner when they seek to obtain vengeance from one mortal man, on whose account they too will be destroyed [?]; for they dared to do such very great things, having risen up against the servants of God;
Because of them, filled with wrath, he will begin to write edicts against all the saints, to slaughter everywhere those who refuse to serve him and worship him as God;

and as Isaiah says: "Woe to that land of ships, wings [?], which sends messengers over the sea and letters of papyrus to perverse nations and to a useless people. In whom does that people trust, which dwells beyond and is trampled upon the earth?"
59. But we who hope in the Son of God are persecuted and oppressed by unbelievers.
For the wings of the ships are the churches, and the sea is this world, in which the church,

like a ship on the sea, is tossed by wintry waves but does not perish, for the skilled master-pilot, Christ, is with her, and she has raised up and holds the conqueror of death, which is the cross of Christ.
For her prow is the east, and her stern the west, and her middle the south, and her two arms are the two commandments,
and the lines stretched around her are the love of Christ, which makes the church firm,
and the cargo, for she carries, as it were, the font of the birth from above, by the renewal of those who believe,
and her shining sail is the Holy Spirit, come down from heaven, by whom those who believe in God are sealed;
next to it there is also an iron anchor [?]: the holy commandments of Christ, which are firm as iron;
and she has sailors on the right and on the left, the holy angels as ministers, who labor continually, and the church stands guarded;
and in her are ladders that lead up and reach to the full height, as a figure of the goings of Christ, to draw the faithful to the ascents of heaven;
and those who spread the sail upon that high mast are the praised ranks of the prophets and apostles and martyrs, who are at rest in the kingdom of Christ.
60. Now, concerning the persecutions and the tribulation that are to come upon the churches, for John too speaks thus:
"And I saw a great and wondrous sign: a woman was clothed with the sun,
and the moon was under her feet, and on her head as a crown were twelve stars; and she cries out with the pains of childbirth and is in anguish to give birth;
and the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth,
so that when she gave birth, he might swallow the son. And she bore a child, who is destined to shepherd all the nations; and her son was caught up to God and to his throne;
and the woman's flight was into the wilderness, where a place has been prepared for her by God, that she may be nourished there one thousand two hundred and sixty days."

"And when the dragon saw this, he persecuted the woman who had borne the child; and to the woman were given two wings as of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness and be nourished there for a time and two times and part of a time, away from the face of that serpent.
And the serpent poured out of his mouth a powerful potion, in order to sweep her away;
and the earth came to the woman's aid, and opened its mouth and swallowed the water which the dragon had poured out of his mouth;
and the dragon was enraged on account of the woman, and went and made war on the rest of her kin, who do the commandment of God and keep the testimonies of Jesus."
61. Now by the woman who was clothed with the sun he plainly means the Church, which has put on the Word of the Father, who is more radiant than the sun.
And when he said, "The moon under her feet," it is because she is adorned with heavenly glory.
And when he said, "Upon her head twelve stars set as a crown," he means the twelve apostles, by whom the Church has been established.

"And being with child she cries out as one giving birth and is in anguish to bear," for she never ceases to bring forth the Word from the heart, even though she is persecuted in the world by unbelievers. And when he said, "She bore a son who is destined to shepherd all the nations," this is the child and perfect Christ,
the Son of God, God, who also appeared to us as man, whom the Church, as if by giving birth, teaches to all the nations.
And when he said, "Her son was snatched up to God and to his throne," it is because he is King of heaven and not from the earth; the Son rejoices through him forever,
as David cries out beforehand and says: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I place your enemies under your feet."
And when he said, "The dragon saw and persecuted the woman who had borne the child,

and two wings as of a great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the wilderness and be nourished there for a time and two times and part of a time, away from the face of the serpent": these are one thousand two hundred and sixty days,
the part of the week in which the assailant will rule, and the days in which he will persecute the churches, for they will be persecuted from city to city and will hide in deserts and mountains.
And when he said, "Two wings as of a great eagle," this is Jesus Christ himself: the hands which he stretched out; on the cross he raised those two wings, right and left,
calling to himself all who believe in him and covering them as a bird covers its chicks;
for he says by the hand of Malachi: "And for you who fear his name the sun of righteousness shall shine forth, and healing under his wings."

62. The Lord himself also says: "When you see the abomination of desolation, that it sits in the holy place — let him who reads understand — at that time let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains,
and let those who are on the rooftops not come down to take anything from their house, and let him who is in the field not turn back to take his garment;
but woe to those who are with child and those who are nursing children in those days,
for at that time there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world, nor will ever be; and if those days were not shortened, no one would be saved."
And Daniel says: "And a sign shall be given to the abomination of desolation, one thousand two hundred and sixty days;
and blessed is he who endures and reaches those days, one thousand three hundred and thirty-five."
63. And the blessed Paul writes to the Thessalonians: "I make known to you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him:
do not be stirred in your mind nor be troubled, neither by spirit nor by word nor by letter as if from us, as though the day of the Lord has now arrived. Let no one [?] deceive you in any way,
unless that deceiver comes first and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the son of perdition,
who rises up in arrogance against all that is called god or any object of worship, until he enters and sits in the temple of God and shows himself as God.
Do you not remember that while I was still with you I told you this very thing? And now we speak [?] of that which stands in the midst, and of his being revealed at his own time.
For the counsel of lawlessness is already now grown strong, and that which now stands remains until it is taken from the midst.
And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom our Lord Jesus Christ will consume and destroy by the manifestation of his coming, the one whose coming is by the power of the devil,
with all power and signs of deceit and wonders of falsehood and with every deception of perdition, because they did not accept the truth of God.
Therefore God will send upon them the spirit of deception, so that they may believe the lie of that liar, and so that all may be judged who did not believe his truth but took pleasure in falsehood."
And Isaiah says: "Let the ungodly one be destroyed, so that he may not see the glory of God."
64. Now concerning these things, beloved, and the division of the one week into two parts, and the foul desolation revealed at that time,

and the completion of their courses by the two prophets and preachers of the Lord, and at the same time the end of the whole world, of those who have existed from then on [?], what will remain, beloved, except the coming from heaven of the Lord and our Savior Christ, the Son of God, for whom we are waiting?
Before him a consuming fire will blaze up, and the judgment of righteousness upon all who did not believe in him.
For the Lord says: "When all these things are about to come to pass, lift up your eyes, for your redemption has drawn near."
"And a hair of your head will not perish."
"For as the lightning flashes forth from the rising of the sun and is seen as far as its setting, so will be the coming of the Son of Man;
for wherever the carcass has fallen, there too the eagles will gather." Now the fall took place in Paradise, from which Adam, having been deceived, fell out.
And again he says: "The Son of Man will send out his angels, and they will gather his elect from the four winds of heaven."

And David shows us beforehand concerning the judgments and concerning the manifestation of the Lord, and he says: "His going forth is from the edge of heaven, and his resting place is at its other edge; and there is no one who can hide from his heat." By heat he means the blazing of the fire. And Isaiah says this: "Go, my people, enter your treasure-chamber, hide for a moment until the wrath of the Lord passes." And Paul says likewise: "For the wrath of God is to be revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and lawlessness of men, who hold the truth of the Lord in falsehood."
65. Now concerning his resurrection and the kingdom of the saints, Daniel says: "And many who are under the earth will rise, some to eternal life and some to reproach and eternal shame."
And Isaiah says: "The dead will arise, and those who are in the tombs will be raised up, for the dew that is from you is healing for them."
And the Lord says: "On that day many will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear it will live."
And the prophet says: "Awake, you who are asleep, rise from the dead, and Christ will give you light."
And John says: "Blessed and holy is the one who has a share in that first resurrection; over such the second death has no power; for that second death is the flame of fire."
For the Lord also says: "At that time the righteous will shine forth like the sun in the kingdom of heaven";
for he will appear in his glory and will say to the saints: "Come, you blessed of my Father, and inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the beginning of the world."
And he will say to the wicked: "Depart, you accursed, into the eternal fire, which has been prepared by my Father for the devil and his angels."
And John says: "Let the adulterers and sorcerers and fornicators and murderers and idolaters depart, and all who practice and love falsehood,
for their portion is the Gehenna of fire." Likewise Isaiah also says:

"They will go out and see the bones of the men who have sinned, for their worm will not cease and their fire will not be quenched, and they will be a spectacle, pointed at by the finger, to all flesh."
66. And Paul writes to the Thessalonians concerning the resurrection of the righteous:
"I do not wish you to be ignorant, brothers, concerning those who have fallen asleep, like the others who have no hope.
If you believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him, by the hand of Jesus, those who have fallen asleep.

This I say to you by the word of the Lord: that you who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, will not precede those who have fallen asleep, for the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a command and with the voice of an angel and with the trumpet of God, and the dead who are in Christ will rise first, and then we who are alive, who remain, will be caught up together with them on the clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so we will be with the Lord at all times."

67. These things, taken in only a small measure from the holy books, like a heavenly crown made of fragrant flowers, I hand over to you, beloved brother Theophilus, so that you may keep these writings in faith, with foreknowledge of the things that have been prepared, without stumbling for yourself, and may preserve them for God and for men, awaiting that blessed hope and the appearing of our Savior God, who will raise up the saints; rejoice together with them, giving glory to the Lord Jesus Christ, whose is the glory forever and ever. Amen.
